notes.text: The Holy Ghost fell on all that were hearing the word — Thus were they consecrated to God, as the first fruits of the Gentiles. And thus did God give a clear and satisfactory evidence, that he had accepted them as well as the Jews.
The believers of the circumcision — The believing Jews.

Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Ghost? — He does not say they have the baptism of the Spirit; therefore they do not need baptism with water. But just the contrary: if they have received the Spirit, then baptize them with water. How easily is this question decided, if we will take the word of God for our rule! Either men have received the Holy Ghost or not. If they have not, Repent, saith God, and be baptized, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost. If they have, if they are already baptized with the Holy Ghost, then who can forbid water?

In the name of the Lord — Which implies the Father who anointed him, and the Spirit with which he was anointed to his office. But as the Gentiles had before believed in God the Father, and could not but now believe in the Holy Ghost, under whose powerful influence they were at this very time, there was the less need of taking notice, that they were baptized into the belief and profession of the sacred Three: though doubtless the apostle administered the ordinances in that very form which Christ himself had prescribed.

glossa.text: *The Spirit.* The Spirit is the house of God, inasmuch as he is given to those who through him love God; but with himself he is God, even if he be given to none, coeternal with the Father and the Son. Nor, because they give, and he himself is given, is he less than they. For he is so given as the gift of God, that he gives himself as God: *For the Spirit breatheth where he will ((Joan. III))*.
*Can any man forbid water,* etc. As if, God first gave what is greater, and inverted the order, can he forbid what is less You have come for this, that you may be witnesses, therefore judge.

*In the name of Christ.* Whereas the rule of the Church is that baptism be delivered in the name of the Trinity, Luke nevertheless testifies that it was given in the name of Jesus Christ. Ambrose, resolving this, says that through the unity of the name the mystery is made full, because he who says Christ designates also the Father, from whom the Son is, and the Holy Spirit: he also who says the Father shows alike both the Son and the Spirit: and he who names the Spirit calls also the Father, from whom the Spirit proceeds, and the Son, whose Spirit he also is. Whence, that authority may be joined to reason, one is baptized also in the Spirit, according to that: *But you shall be baptized in the Holy Spirit ((Act. XI))*, and the Apostle: *In one Spirit we have been baptized ((I Cor. XII))*.

notes.text: Salvation — The redemption of the world by the Messiah: which was hitherto reserved was a secret among the Jews, yea was not throughly known by the most of the Jews themselves. Righteousness - His faithfulness in accomplishing this great promise. Israel is required to praise God, for their hasty constitution both in church and state, ver. 1-5. Some instances of the happy administration of it, ver. 6-9.

glossa.text:
*Sing ye to the Lord.* ((CASS.)) First he speaks of the showing forth of the saving right hand.

*He hath saved.* ((AUG.)) It is a greater thing that he raised up the whole world from eternal death, than that he raised the dead. *To himself.* Many are saved bodily, but to themselves, not to him: they who, having received bodily health, grow wanton, but they who by faith are healed within, are healed to him, or save themselves.

*Salvation . . . justice.* ((AUG.)) He who saves and justifies. *He hath revealed.* Things to come were foretold under a veil by the prophets: but the veil has been taken away, since *truth is sprung out of the earth.*

*Of mercy and of truth.* ((AUG.)) *Mercy* is that whereby he promised, *truth* follows upon this, because he rendered it. But to whom? *To Israel,* that is, to him who now by faith sees the truth, afterwards by sight.
*All.* ((ID.)) Because Christ was not given to certain men only.
*Rejoice ye.* ((CASS.)) Secondly he says that in all ways he is to be praised and declared, because the judge is come.

*With ductile trumpets and with the voice of a trumpet of horn.* ((AUG.)) Of brass, which are drawn out by beating, etc., *as far as* as the horn cleaves to the flesh, and surpasses it. ((HIERON.)) With ductile trumpets, of silver, after the manner of the Jews. Mystically, drawn out under the hammer of the whole earth, that is, the devil. ((AUG.)) Tribulation is the beating; advancement, the drawing out: such a trumpet was Job, whence he sounded as a trumpet, saying: *The Lord gave, the Lord hath taken away.*

*Let it be moved.* ((ID.)) That is, let the sea of the law be made sweet, the wood of the cross being set therein. *And the fulness thereof.* All the sacraments of the law, etc., *as far as* but *the rivers,* etc. *The earth.* ((CASS.)) That is, every sinner.

*The world of the earth.* All earthly men. *In justice.* ((AUG.)) Because they did not merit mercy. *The peoples.* ((CASS.)) The faithful out of the Jews and the Gentiles, who shall receive things equal to their merits.

notes.text: The scope and sum of this whole paragraph appears from the conclusion of it, 1 John v, xiii, "These things have I written to you who believe, that ye may know that ye who believe have eternal life." So faith is the first and last point with St. John also. Every one who loveth — God that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him - Hath a natural affection to all his brethren.
Hereby we know — This is a plain proof. That we love the children of God - As his children.
For this is the love of God — The only sure proof of it. That we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous - To any that are born of God.

For whatsoever — This expression implies the most unlimited universality. Is born of God overcometh the world - Conquers whatever it can lay in the way, either to allure or fright the children of God from keeping his commandments. And this is the victory - The grand means of overcoming. Even our faith - Seeing all things are possible to him that believeth.

Who is he that overcometh the world — That is superior to all worldly care, desire, fear? Every believer, and none else. The seventh verse (usually so reckoned) is a brief recapitulation of all which has been before advanced concerning the Father, the Son, and the Spirit. It is cited, in conjunction with the sixth and eighth, 1 John v, 6, 8 by Tertullian, Cyprian, and an uninterrupted train of Fathers. And, indeed, what the sun is in the world, what the heart is in a man, what the needle is in the mariner's compass, this verse is in the epistle. By this the sixth, eighth, and ninth verses 1 John v, 6, 8, 9 are indissolubly connected; as will be evident, beyond all contradiction, when they are accurately considered.

This is he — St. John here shows the immovable foundation of that faith that Jesus is the Son of God; not only the testimony of man, but the firm, indubitable testimony of God. Who came - Jesus is he of whom it was promised that he should come; and who accordingly, is come. And this the Spirit, and the water, and the blood testify. Even Jesus - Who, coming by water and blood, is by this very thing demonstrated to be the Christ. Not by the water only - Wherein he was baptized. But by the water and the blood - Which he shed when he had finished the work his Father had given him to do. He not only undertook at his baptism "to fulfil all righteousness," but on the cross accomplished what he had undertaken; in token whereof, when all was finished, blood and water came out of his side. And it is the Spirit who likewise testifieth - Of Jesus Christ, namely, by Moses and all the prophets, by John the Baptist, by all the apostles, and in all the writings of the New Testament. And against his testimony there can be no exception, because the Spirit is truth - The very God of truth.

glossa.text: *Every one that believeth.* He believes who so lives as Christ commanded, otherwise the devils also believe. But works apart from faith are either nothing, or, even if they seem good, are empty, because they are apart from the way, which is Christ. Truly he who loves God loves his brother. For he who loves God the Father loves God the Son, begotten of the Father, and he who loves God the Son loves also the sons of God, the members of that head.

*They are not heavy. ((BEDA.))* They do not draw downward, like a talent of lead, etc., *as far as* lest anyone should trust that by his own strength he can overcome the world, he adds concerning faith:
*And this is the victory,* etc. That faith, namely, which works through love, which craves God's help.

*But who is he?* etc. He determines what faith conquers, namely the faith of Christ. As if to say: Truly through faith he conquers the world, because through anything else it is not conquered. *Our faith.* Behold what faith conquers, that which believes him true man and true God.

*This is he,* etc. Because faith and the confession of the divinity alone does not suffice for salvation and for overcoming the world, he adds also concerning the humanity: therefore he expressed the blood.

*The spirit.* That is, the human soul which he gave up in the passion; *water and blood,* which flowed from his side. This could not have been done, if he had not had the true nature of flesh. But even before the passion, the sweat which was made like drops of blood showed the truth of the flesh. And this, that from the side of one already dead, against nature, water, blood flowed vigorously, bore witness that the body of the Lord would live better after death, and that his death would give us life. But that the sweat flowed like blood onto the earth signified that he would wash the Church in the whole world with his own blood.

notes.text: Abide ye in my love — Keep your place in my affection. See that ye do not forfeit that invaluable blessing. How needless a caution, if it were impossible for them not to abide therein?
If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love — On these terms, and no other, ye shall remain the objects of my special affection.
That my joy might remain in you — The same joy which I feel in loving the Father, and keeping his commandments.
Your joy will be full, if ye so love one another.
Greater love — To his friends. He here speaks of them only.
Ye are my friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you — On this condition, not otherwise. A thunderbolt for Antinomianism! Who then dares assert that God's love does not at all depend on man's works?
All things — Which might be of service to you.

Ye — My apostles, have not chosen me, but I have chosen you - As clearly appears from the sacred history: and appointed you, that ye may go and bear fruit - I have chosen and appointed you for this end, that ye may go and convert sinners: and that your fruit may remain - That the fruit of your labours may remain to the end of the world; yea, to eternity; that whatsoever ye shall ask - The consequence of your going and bearing fruit will be, that all your prayers will be heard.

glossa.text: *That joy.* The joy of God concerning us, whom he foreknew and predestined, is always full; in us it begins from faith, it grows, nay and shall be perfected in the resurrection.

*This is the commandment,* etc. And above concerning love toward the neighbour; but repetition is confirmation: there, however, he says, I give a commandment, as though it had not been before; but here, this is, as though it were not another. There, New, lest we remain in oldness; here, Mine, lest it be contemned.
*Greater than this.* He defines the fulness of mutual love which he commands them to have.

*Now I will not call.* Love having been commended, he adds what belongs to condescension, that he should call good servants (who know by doing the things he commands) friends, and takes from them the name of servant, which is from fear, by casting it out, [the servant] who does not know what his Lord does. Because when he does anything, he is so exalted as though he himself did it, and not the lord.

*These things I command,* etc. Here he shows what is the fruit of which he had spoken, for which the Father will also give what we ask, who gave this also, that we should love.

*That you love one another. ((AUG.))* Deservedly does he often commend love, as though it alone were to be commanded, without which the rest cannot be, and which without the rest cannot be had. And for its sake we ought patiently to endure even all the adversities of the world. Whence he subjoins:

This is the Spirit's entry now

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions. And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.
echoes.note: 'The gift of the Holy Spirit was also poured out on the Gentiles' fulfills 'I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh' — the same Joel oracle already cited at Pentecost (recurrence within Acts), now extended to 'all flesh' inclusive of Gentiles. High coherence; the pouring-out language is distinctive.

echoes.text: For I will pour water on him who is thirsty, and streams on the dry ground. I will pour my Spirit on your seed, and my blessing on your offspring:
echoes.note: 'I will pour my Spirit upon your seed' provides a parallel outpouring-of-the-Spirit promise reinforcing the Joel intertext behind v45. Moderate verbal overlap.

echoes.text: neither will I hide my face any more from them; for I have poured out my Spirit on the house of Israel, says the Lord Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'I have poured out my Spirit upon the house of Israel' is a further prophetic pour-out text in the background of the Spirit falling on the hearers. Faint.

echoes.text: Until the Spirit is poured on us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is considered a forest.
echoes.note: 'Until the Spirit be poured upon us from on high' contributes to the prophetic expectation of the Spirit's outpouring realized here on the Gentiles.

echoes.text: The whole earth was of one language and of one speech. As they traveled east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and they lived there. They said one to another, “Come, let’s make bricks, and burn them thoroughly.” They had brick for stone, and they used tar for mortar. They said, “Come, let’s build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top reaches to the sky, and let’s make ourselves a name, lest we be scattered abroad on the surface of the whole […]
echoes.note: The Gentiles 'speaking in other languages and magnifying God' figurally reverses Babel's scattering of tongues, with diverse speech now uniting in praise. Typological, no verbal borrowing.

spans.label: Tarsus & Antioch
spans.note: Sent home to Tarsus, then fetched by Barnabas to teach at Antioch, where the disciples were first called Christians. Ends with the famine-relief visit to Jerusalem.

places.name: Caesarea
places.id: On the Mediterranean coast c. 60 km northwest of Jerusalem, on the site of an earlier Hellenistic Strato's Tower. Rebuilt by Herod the Great as a deepwater harbor with concrete moles, an aqueduct from Mount Carmel, and a temple to Roma and Augustus. The administrative capital of Roman Judea/Palaestina from c. 6 A.D. Distinct from Caesarea Philippi (Banias) at the foot of Mount Hermon.

places.name: Joppa
places.id: Tel Yafo (Jaffa) on the Mediterranean coast, the natural harbor for Jerusalem. Listed in Thutmose III's Karnak topographical list and in the Amarna letters.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.id: The City of David and Old City, on the spurs above the Kidron Valley, c. 50 km from the Mediterranean. Pre-Israelite Jebus; named here as the seat of Adoni-Zedek, leader of the southern coalition.

places.name: Judea
places.id: The Roman administrative province (later procuratorial province) covering the southern hill country of Israel — Jerusalem, the Judean wilderness, and territory south to the Negev. The Greco-Roman successor to the Hasmonean and Herodian Iudaea. Pin sits in the central hill country.

places.name: Galilee
places.id: The northern region of Roman-period Palestine, bounded by the Jezreel valley (south), the Lebanese mountains (north), the Mediterranean (west), and the Jordan / Sea of Galilee (east). Subdivided into Lower Galilee (the Jesus traditions are mostly here) and Upper Galilee.

places.name: Nazareth
places.id: Modern en-Nasira / Nazareth in Lower Galilee, c. 30 km west of the Sea of Galilee. A village of perhaps 200-400 in the early first century, identified through continuous habitation, tomb evidence, and the third-century Caesarea inscription naming it as a priestly course settlement.

echoes.text: You shall love Yahweh your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.
echoes.note: The Shema's command to love God with the whole self stands behind 'when we love God and keep his commandments.' John makes love of God inseparable from obedience, exactly the link Deuteronomy forges. Loving God and keeping commandments are presented as a single covenantal disposition.

echoes.text: For this commandment which I command you this day is not too hard for you or too distant.
echoes.note: 'His commandments are not grievous' closely echoes Moses' insistence that 'this commandment which I command you this day is not too hard for you, neither is it far off.' Both texts answer an anticipated objection that God's law is an unbearable weight. The shared logic is that those rightly related to God find his demands livable, not crushing.

echoes.text: Know therefore that Yahweh your God himself is God, the faithful God, who keeps covenant and loving kindness with them who love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations,
echoes.note: The pairing of loving God with keeping his commandments matches the covenant formula describing God's faithfulness to 'them that love him and keep his commandments.' John inverts the perspective to the believer's side but preserves the same Deuteronomic word-pair. The covenantal idiom of love-plus-obedience is distinctively Mosaic.

echoes.text: Yahweh your God will circumcise your heart, and the heart of your seed, to love Yahweh your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, that you may live.
echoes.note: The promise that God will 'circumcise your heart... to love the LORD your God' anticipates John's notion that the one born of God both believes and loves. The new birth that produces obedient love develops the Deuteronomic hope of an inwardly transformed, God-loving heart. Both locate the capacity to love God in a divine act upon the person.

echoes.text: Sing to Yahweh a new song, for he has done marvelous things! His right hand, and his holy arm, have worked salvation for him.
echoes.note: 'This is the victory that has overcome the world' draws on the psalmic celebration that God's 'right hand and his holy arm hath gotten him the victory.' The vocabulary of decisive divine victory is transferred to faith's triumph over the world. The believer shares in a conquest that is ultimately God's own.

echoes.text: For they didn’t get the land in possession by their own sword, neither did their own arm save them; but your right hand, and your arm, and the light of your face, because you were favorable to them.
echoes.note: The motif that victory comes 'not by their own sword' but by God's arm and favor underlies John's claim that the overcoming power is faith rather than human strength. The world is conquered by a God-given means, not by force. The echo is faint and thematic.

echoes.text: I will delight myself in your commandments, because I love them.
echoes.note: The psalmist's delight in commandments he loves complements John's claim that God's commandments 'are not grievous.' Both portray the law as an object of love rather than burden. The connection is conceptual, supporting the un-burdensome framing of obedience.

echoes.text: My son, don’t forget my teaching; but let your heart keep my commandments:
echoes.note: The wisdom appeal to keep the father's commandments in the heart parallels John's keeping-commandments-as-love. Proverbs frames obedience as life-giving rather than oppressive. A faint sapiential backdrop to John's gentle yoke.

echoes.text: One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, or for any sin, in any sin that he sins. At the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall a matter be established.
echoes.note: 'There are three who testify... and the three agree as one' applies the Mosaic rule that a matter is established 'at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses.' John assembles exactly the legally sufficient number of corroborating witnesses to validate the testimony about the Son. The juridical framework of accredited witnesses is drawn straight from the Torah's evidentiary law.

echoes.text: At the mouth of two witnesses, or three witnesses, he who is to die shall be put to death. At the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death.
echoes.note: The companion legal principle requiring multiple witnesses to establish a capital matter reinforces John's threefold testimony. The Spirit, water, and blood function as the plurality of witnesses that secures conviction in God's case for his Son. The forensic logic of confirmed testimony is Deuteronomic.

echoes.text: “‘Whoever kills any person, the murderer shall be slain at the mouth of witnesses; but one witness shall not testify against any person that he die.
echoes.note: The legal insistence that no single witness suffices, but a plurality establishes the verdict, undergirds John's grouping of three concurring witnesses. The motif that life-and-death matters demand corroborated testimony fits John's life-giving testimony about the Son. A further Pentateuchal source for the witness-rule.

echoes.text: For the life of the flesh is in the blood; and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that makes atonement by reason of the life.
echoes.note: The blood among the witnesses evokes the Levitical principle that 'the life of the flesh is in the blood' and that blood makes atonement. John's 'water and blood' draws atoning significance from the sacrificial system where blood is the witnessing, life-bearing agent. The blood testifies because it is the locus of atoning life.

echoes.text: “You are my witnesses,” says Yahweh, “With my servant whom I have chosen; that you may know and believe me, and understand that I am he. Before me there was no God formed, neither will there be after me.
echoes.note: God's declaration 'Ye are my witnesses... that ye may know and believe me' parallels John's structure of divine testimony aimed at belief and knowledge of God. The 'testimony of God' that one must receive develops Isaiah's courtroom scenes where God testifies to himself. Both stage a trial in which God's own witness compels faith.

echoes.text: He shall take some of the blood of the bull, and sprinkle it with his finger on the mercy seat on the east; and before the mercy seat he shall sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times.
echoes.note: The Day of Atonement sprinkling of blood stands behind the atoning weight John gives 'the blood.' The cleansing blood ritual informs the salvific testimony of Christ's blood. A faint cultic resonance underlying the witness of blood.

echoes.text: “A man who is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer, and lay them up outside of the camp in a clean place; and it shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Israel for a water for impurity. It is a sin offering.
echoes.note: The 'water of purification' from the red heifer informs the cleansing connotation of 'the water' among the witnesses. Purifying water and atoning blood together echo the Pentateuchal rites of cleansing. The pairing of water and blood recalls Israel's purification system.

echoes.text: Moses took half of the blood and put it in basins, and half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar. He took the book of the covenant and read it in the hearing of the people, and they said, “All that Yahweh has spoken will we do, and be obedient.” Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, “Look, this is the blood of the covenant, which Yahweh has made with you concerning all these words.”
echoes.note: The covenant ratification in which Moses applies the blood and the people pledge obedience associates blood with sealed testimony. John's blood-witness to the Son parallels the blood that confirmed the covenant. A faint covenantal-blood backdrop to the witnessing blood.

echoes.text: Turn your ear, and come to me; hear, and your soul shall live: and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David.
echoes.note: The offer of 'an everlasting covenant... the sure mercies of David' and the call to 'hear, and your soul shall live' resonate with John's 'God gave to us eternal life.' Hearing God's testimony issues in life. A faint resonance for life granted through receiving God's word.

echoes.text: For whoever finds me, finds life, and will obtain favor from Yahweh.
echoes.note: Wisdom's promise 'whoso findeth me findeth life' parallels 'He who has the Son has the life.' Possessing the divine gift is possessing life itself. A sapiential echo for life located in a person to be found.

echoes.text: For wisdom is a spirit that loves man, And she will not hold a blasphemer guiltless for his lips; Because God bears witness of his reins, And is a true overseer of his heart, And a hearer of his tongue:
echoes.note: The portrayal of the Spirit as a witness who searches and testifies of inward truth resonates with 'It is the Spirit who testifies, because the Spirit is the truth.' The deuterocanonical conception of the Spirit as truthful witness anticipates John's Spirit-testimony. The connection is thematic and faint.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: “But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend,
echoes.note: 'Abraham my friend' (lit. the one who loved me) — the title 'friend of God' Jesus confers, 'I have called you friends' (15:14-15). The friendship/election language ('Israel... whom I have chosen, offspring of Abraham my friend') gives high availability and coherence to the friend motif.

echoes.text: For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God. Yahweh your God has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth. Yahweh didn’t set his love on you, nor choose you, because you were more in number than any people; for you were the fewest of all peoples: but because Yahweh loves you, and because he desires to keep the oath which he swore to your fathers, Yahweh has brought you out with a mighty hand, […]
echoes.note: 'You did not choose me, but I chose you' (15:16) echoes Israel's election: the Lord chose them not for their merit but in love. Strong coherence on divine election and love; covenantal keeping of commandments (15:10) belongs to the same Deuteronomic frame.

echoes.text: Didn’t you, our God, drive out the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel, and give it to the seed of Abraham your friend forever?
echoes.note: 'Abraham your friend' — second OT witness to the Abraham-as-friend-of-God title that 'you are my friends' (15:14) actualizes for the disciples. Recurrence with Isa 41:8 strengthens the friend-of-God tradition behind the saying.

echoes.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. He turned again into the camp, but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, didn’t depart from the Tent.
echoes.note: The Lord spoke to Moses 'as a man speaks to his friend' — the paradigm of intimate friendship with God in which the friend is told the divine purposes, matching 15:15: not servants but friends, 'for everything I heard from my Father I have made known to you.'

echoes.text: Yahweh said, “Will I hide from Abraham what I do, since Abraham has surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed in him? For I have known him, to the end that he may command his children and his household after him, that they may keep the way of Yahweh, to do righteousness and justice; to the end that Yahweh may bring on Abraham that which he has spoken of him.”
echoes.note: 'Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?' — the friend of God is not kept ignorant of the master's plans, precisely the logic of 15:15 ('the servant doesn't know what his lord does... I have made known to you'). Coherence with the friend-vs-servant distinction.

echoes.text: “‘You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'Love your neighbor as yourself' underlies the new commandment to 'love one another' (15:12,17). Availability and thematic coherence are strong, though Jesus reframes the measure as 'as I have loved you.'

echoes.text: When he had made an end of speaking to Saul, the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul. Saul took him that day, and would let him go no more home to his father’s house. Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.
echoes.note: Jonathan's covenant love for David, loving him 'as his own soul' and risking his life, is the paradigmatic OT instance of self-giving friendship behind 'greater love has no one than to lay down his life for his friends' (15:13). Faint but coherent.

echoes.text: Let me sing for my well beloved a song of my beloved about his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a very fruitful hill. He dug it up, gathered out its stones, planted it with the choicest vine, built a tower in its midst, and also cut out a wine press therein. He looked for it to yield grapes, but it yielded wild grapes. “Now, inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, please judge between me and my vineyard. What could have been done more to my […]
echoes.note: The vineyard the Beloved tends out of love continues from 15:1-8 into the love/fruit language here (15:9-16); election to 'go and bear fruit that should remain' recalls God's purpose for his loved vineyard. Secondary recurrence of the chapter's controlling image.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Sing something new this morning, you whom God has chosen, for the old griefs do not get the last word.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
He no longer calls you servant, kept at arm's length; he calls you friend, and tells you everything.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
He says, Abide in my love, and let my joy be in you, and let your joy be full.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
So love one another the way he first loved you, and watch the Spirit fall on every kind of person.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Sing to the Lord a new song.

Christ is risen, Alleluia!
Abide in his love; let your joy be full.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
Come, let us love as we are loved.
We are his friends. Alleluia!
